display.purpose: The one large title per view. 34px from md; 28px (Directory) to 30px (other views) on phones.

headline.purpose: Card titles such as the report form header.

title.purpose: A selected item heading, such as the selected country on the map.

row-title.purpose: Country names in list rows; input text at 16px to prevent iOS zoom.

body.purpose: Subtitles (max 60ch), detail values, chat messages, embassy rows.

body-small.purpose: Report text, empty-state support copy; chip labels at weight 500.

footnote.purpose: Row secondary lines (stay, dated report recency), counts, disclaimers.

section-label.purpose: Sentence-case section headings in detail panels and A to Z letter headers.

shadows.name: stuck-edge

shadows.name: floating-control

shadows.name: popover
shadows.purpose: Desktop map hover tooltip. The largest shadow in the system.

shadows.name: segment-thumb
shadows.purpose: Selected segment in a segmented control.

motion.name: disclosure
motion.purpose: Row grows open in place, 0fr to 1fr. Removed under reduced motion.

motion.name: chevron-rotate

motion.name: state-color

breakpoints.name: sm

breakpoints.name: md
breakpoints.purpose: Tabs move into the header; bottom tab bar hides; rows gain stay and report columns.

breakpoints.name: lg
breakpoints.purpose: Stories splits 5/7 with a sticky form.

extensions.darkMode: All colour tokens switch via @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) on :root; colorMeta.<key>.dark holds each dark value. theme-color meta: #ffffff light, #181a1f dark.
extensions.focus: Global :focus-visible outline 2px solid rgb(var(--accent)), offset 2px. Fields replace it with a 2px accent ring at 40%. Selection background rgb(var(--accent) / 0.22). Caret accent.
extensions.iconography: One drawn line family: 24px viewBox, stroke currentColor, stroke-width 1.75, round caps and joins. Sizes 16px inline, 18px fields and mark, 24px tab bar.

narrative.northStar: The Settings Pane for the World
narrative.overview:
The site is a system list, not a themed destination. Every surface reads like a well-made settings or reference pane: a pale grouped ground, white inset-grouped lists, hairline separators, system UI type, and exactly one blue for selection and links. The craft bar is Stripe Docs and Dashboard for density and typographic discipline, Apple Settings and Health for grouped lists and the phone-first tab bar. Nothing is decorative; the only colour beyond the accent is the five status tints, and they are information.

Density is moderate and phone-first: rows are 52px tall, about eight countries show above the tab bar, and a row grows open in place instead of navigating away. Desktop widens the same list into columns rather than inventing a second layout. Dark mode is a mirror, not a separate theme: every token has a dark counterpart switched by the system setting, never by a toggle.

This world explicitly replaces the previous near-black dashboard with glowing chips, gradient text, glass panels and emoji chrome. None of those return.
keyCharacteristics: Grouped ground plus white inset-grouped lists, hairline-separated, 12px group corners.
System font stack only; hierarchy by size and weight, never by case or tracking tricks.
One accent (blue) for selection, links and the primary action; status colour lives only in pills and map fills.
Drawn line icons from one family (24px grid, 1.75 stroke, round caps); flags are content, not chrome.
Flat at rest; small shadows only on things that float above the page.
Disclosure in place: one row open at a time, height animates, nothing re-mounts.

rules.name: The One Blue Rule
rules.body: The accent is the only interactive colour. If something is selected, linked or the primary action, it is blue; if it is not, it is neutral. No second accent, no gradient, no glow.

rules.name: The Status-Is-Data Rule
rules.body: Status hues appear only where they mean a visa status (pill, map fill, legend swatch) or a form outcome (error red, success green). Never use them for decoration, category colour or emphasis.

rules.name: The Mirror Rule
rules.body: Every colour is a token with a light and dark value switched by `prefers-color-scheme`. A raw hex in a component is a bug; the one exception is the Telegram mark, which keeps its own brand blue.

rules.name: The Sentence-Case Rule
rules.body: Labels and section headings are sentence case at 13px semibold in ink-secondary or ink-tertiary. No uppercase, no wide tracking, no eyebrow line above a title.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Counts, stays and dates use tabular figures so columns of numbers align.

rules.name: The Flat-Ground Rule
rules.body: Lists, cards and bars never cast shadows. If it sits in the page flow, it is separated by a hairline; only floating things get a shadow, and never larger than the popover value.

dos: **Do** put every list in a white inset group on the grouped ground, with hairlines inset to the text column (52px).
**Do** render status only through the shared pill and map fills, using the canonical five labels.
**Do** date every community report line ("3 reports · 2 wk ago") in the footnote style.
**Do** expand detail in place with the 280ms disclosure; keep one row open at a time.
**Do** use the system font stack, sentence case, and tabular figures for counts and stays.
**Do** draw icons from the single line family (24px grid, 1.75 stroke, round caps).
**Do** define every new colour as an RGB-channel token with a light and a dark value.
**Do** keep the large title plus one-line subtitle as the opening of every view.
donts: **Don't** bring back the old look: near-black dashboard, glowing chips, gradient text, glass or backdrop blur, coloured drop shadows.
**Don't** use emoji as interface icons in navigation, buttons or headers; flags inside country rows are content and stay.
**Don't** add a second accent colour or use status hues for decoration.
**Don't** cast shadows on in-flow surfaces; reserve the four shadow values for floating elements.
**Don't** use uppercase labels, wide letter-spacing, or an eyebrow line above titles.
**Don't** load a web font or a display face; the system stack is the brand.
**Don't** hard-code hex or Tailwind palette colours (zinc, blue-600 and so on) in components.
